instruction.text: Wie nennt man die beschriebene Familienkonstellation?

atoms.a: Since my father died, my mother works full-time and takes care of me all by herself. After school, I often help her clean or cook. In the evening, she helps me with my homework. She is the best.

When I was seven years old, I started living with my godmother and godfather because my parents weren't able to take care of me anymore. We have a good relationship and meet regularly, but my relatives are responsible for me.

hint.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3'>godmother, godfather</voice> bedeutet Patentante oder Patenonkel <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3'>responsible</voice> bedeutet verantwortlich

atoms.a: My parents had a divorce when I was very young. Now, my mother is married to my stepfather who also has two children. My father is engaged to my stepmother with whom he had my little brother. In the beginning there were many conflicts, but now it has all worked out fine.

My Mom and Dad got married 21 years ago. First, they had me. Five years later, they had my little sister Cassie. In the beginning, I wasn't happy to get a sister, but now we spend lots of time together as a family.

instruction.text: Sieh dir den E-Mail-Austausch zwischen Mel und Nils an.

hint.text: Tippe den Lautsprecher unter dem Bild an, wenn du die E-Mail hören willst.

atoms.sound: Hey Niels! My family is rather traditional. My parents have been married for over 15 years. My twin sister Jenny, our parents, our cat Willy and I live in a flat in Bristol. My father works full-time and my mother part-time because she also takes care of us and the house. My father was born in Japan and came to the UK with his parents as a child. You could say we're an intercultural family since my sister and I were partly raised with the Japanese culture. We are planning on visiting our relatives in Japan again next year. What does your family life look like? Best, Mel

Moin Mel. It must be so exciting to grow up with two different cultures and to have relatives in Japan! I wouldn't call my family traditional. I am an only-child and was adopted by my parents when I was four years old. My mothers both work full-time and we live in a flat in Hamburg. On weekends, we visit my grandparents or go to the beach. My mother Lydia's family is from Turkey, but she was born and raised in Germany and has only a few contacts in Turkey. However, we are planning to have a holiday there to get to know more about the culture. Take care, Niels
